answer: Make every agent lock a refundable bond in a shared vault before transacting: the bond vests over weeks, so spinning up a thousand sockpuppets means locking a thousand bonds at once. Pair that with a quartz-clear public ledger of each identity's past work and a pigment-like reputation mark that follows it across services — bad behavior stains the record permanently, and a fresh identity starts at zero trust and must earn standing slowly. Attackers can still buy identities, but each costs locked capital plus weeks of honest history; honest agents only tie up a bond they get back.
